text:
Zoe Park: Quick note: brought up anchovy-embed-v0.9-small in canary. Topline: recall@10 only -0.8% vs prod, but recall@1 for 1-2 token queries tanked ~7.5%. Noticed different cluster shape in low-dim viz. :confused:
Marcus Li: wow that's specific to 1-2 token queries? any obvious tokenization or pooling change in v0.9?
Zoe Park: v0.9 moved to a lightweight attn-pooler + layer scale tweak. Tokenizer unchanged. I exported a UMAP of the holdout (attached): https://artifacts.redwood/anchovy/umap_canary_2026-03-21.png
Juniper Rao: can you paste the eval command? want to reproduce locally.
Zoe Park: run used: ```bash
./run_eval --model anchovy-embed-v0.9 --dataset holdout-shorttail --k 1,5,10 --pool attn --normalize l2```
Tom B.: Did you try mean pooling baseline to confirm attn-pool is the culprit?
Zoe Park: mean-pool baseline in staging gives recall@1 much closer to prod (only -1.2%). So attn-pool is suspect.
Marcus Li: check token embedding norms and per-token L2 shifts; short queries rely on one token so any token-scale drift will show up big.
eval-bot: token-norm-diff scan complete. Top short tokens increased norm: ["ok","now","api","err"] with median +9%.
Juniper Rao: +9% token norms on common short tokens explains much of the displacement. Are these tokens more frequent in the new fine-tune mix?
Zoe Park: possible, v0.9 fine-tune included more logs/snippet examples. Also tried disabling final L2 norm — made negligible difference.
Tom B.: Could attention pooling be underweighting single-token signals because of learned position bias? Dump some attn weights for 1-2 token examples.
Zoe Park: sample: ```text
["q":"api", "attn": [0.03,0.94,0.03]]
["q":"ok", "attn": [0.15,0.70,0.15]]
```
Marcus Li: those look fine for single token, but if token emb norms are scaled up it will push the pooled vector off-center. Try mean-centering token vectors before pooling.
Zoe Park: ran a quick patch: mean-center tokens before attn-pool (vecs = vecs - vecs.mean(axis=0)). Quick scan: recall@1 on 1-2 token bucket improved from 38.4% -> 44.9% (prod baseline 46.2%). Overall recall@10 stable.
eval-bot: quick-run summary: anchovy-v0.9 attn w/mean-center: recall@1=44.9%, recall@5=71.3%, recall@10=79.0%. anchovy-v0.9 attn raw: recall@1=38.4%. prod baseline recall@1=46.2%.
Juniper Rao: good. Two paths: small postproc (mean-center) or small contrastive calibration on token table to nudge norms down. Which is faster to ship?
Tom B.: postproc is fastest but let's validate on quantized builds — int8 often exaggerates scale mismatches.
Zoe Park: tried ONNX int8 quick export; raw attn int8 recall@1 dropped further to 33.0%. Attn+mean-center int8 -> 39.5%. Still behind.
Marcus Li: then calibration may be necessary for quant parity. Try a tiny contrastive LR on token embeddings for 50k short examples, freeze rest. Also sweep attention temperature (0.2, 0.5, 1.0) to see if scaling helps.
Juniper Rao: also run silhouette score and intra-cluster cosine variance for short bucket to quantify fragmentation.
Zoe Park: added tasks to the issue: https://github.com/redwood/anchovy/issues/89. Will push eval logs and UMAPs there.
eval-bot: silhouette short-bucket: prod=0.40, anchovy-v0.9 attn=0.29, attn+mean-center=0.34.
Tom B.: assign follow-ups: Marcus to run contrastive micro-calib + quant builds, Juniper to sweep attn-temp + pool ablations, Zoe to open PR for optional postproc flag and attach artifacts. Can we canary postproc on 2%?
Zoe Park: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/anchovy/pull/201 adding `--postproc mean_center_tokens=true`. Will include perf runs.
Marcus Li: I'll post calibration + int8 results by EOD. If calibration brings int8 within 2% of prod, prefer that over postproc.
Zoe Park: thanks team. Closing for now; will update issue with the calibration results and canary plan. :white_check_mark:
